package_info.why_malicious: All packages in this campaign contain intentionally obfuscated JavaScript that, upon installation or test execution, launches a reverse shell to a remote attacker-controlled server (rsh.51pwn.com:8880), exfiltrating detailed system and environment information. The attack is triggered via multiple npm lifecycle hooks (preinstall, postinstall, test, and custom init), ensuring execution in a variety of scenarios. The code employs anti-analysis techniques, such as disabling NODE_NO_EVAL and using compressed, in-memory payloads, indicating clear malicious intent and evasion of detection.

execution_context.trigger: During npm install, test, or init script execution (preinstall, postinstall, test, and custom init hooks)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During npm install, test, or init script execution, the package runs ./scripts/init.js via multiple npm lifecycle hooks, invoking the same script in detached mode to maximize execution opportunities, resulting in the launch of the malicious payload regardless of how the package is used.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate packages rarely execute custom scripts on install, and almost never on both preinstall and postinstall, as well as test and custom init hooks. This maximizes the chance of malicious code execution and increases the attack surface.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not execute arbitrary scripts on install or test without clear user intent, and do not use multiple lifecycle hooks to trigger the same script.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages may use install hooks for build steps, but not for launching detached processes or obfuscated payloads, and not across all lifecycle hooks simultaneously.
key_indicators: Multiple npm lifecycle hooks (preinstall, postinstall, test, init) all pointing to the same script
Use of background execution ('&') to detach process
Absence of legitimate build or setup logic in scripts

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When ./scripts/init.js is executed, the script forks a new detached process running scripts/rsh.js and immediately exits, allowing the malicious payload to persist independently and evade process monitoring.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Forking a detached process from an install/test script is highly unusual and is a common technique to evade process monitoring and ensure persistence of malicious activity.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal install/test scripts do not spawn detached child processes, especially not to run further scripts without user interaction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate daemons or background services might use this, but not in npm install scripts or in this context.
key_indicators: Detached child process creation using child_process.fork with {detached: true}
Immediate process exit after forking to hide parent process activity

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When scripts/rsh.js is executed, the code collects extensive system and environment information, compresses it, decompresses an obfuscated payload, disables NODE_NO_EVAL, and executes the payload via eval, resulting in the establishment of a reverse shell and exfiltration of collected data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script is heavily obfuscated, collects sensitive system and environment data, and uses eval to execute a decompressed, hidden payload. The use of compression, obfuscation, and eval is a hallmark of malicious code designed to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal scripts do not collect and exfiltrate system information, nor do they execute obfuscated payloads via eval, especially during install or test phases.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Compression and system info gathering may be used in diagnostics, but not in install scripts or with obfuscated payloads and eval.
key_indicators: Systematic collection of sensitive system and environment data
Use of eval on decompressed, hidden code

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the in-memory payload is executed, the code establishes a persistent reverse shell to rsh.51pwn.com:8880, sends a marker and the compressed system data, and provides the attacker with remote shell access, automatically reconnecting if the connection is lost.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing a reverse shell to an external server, exfiltrating system data, and implementing persistent reconnection logic is a classic remote access trojan (RAT) behavior, enabling full attacker control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should open a reverse shell or exfiltrate data on install or test, nor should it maintain persistent outbound connections to attacker infrastructure.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; reverse shells and persistent C2 connections are never legitimate in package install/test scripts.
key_indicators: Reverse shell logic using net.Socket and child_process.spawn
Exfiltration of system/environment data with unique marker ('51pwn_npm')

attack_chain.action: Malicious npm package is installed or test/init script is run, triggering execution of ./scripts/init.js via multiple npm lifecycle hooks (preinstall, postinstall, test, init).
init.js forks a detached process to run scripts/rsh.js, then exits to evade detection and allow the payload to persist independently.
scripts/rsh.js collects system and environment data, compresses it, decompresses and executes an obfuscated payload via eval, and disables NODE_NO_EVAL for anti-analysis.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of in-memory reverse shell payload

attack_chain.action: The in-memory payload establishes a reverse shell to rsh.51pwn.com:8880, exfiltrates system data, and provides persistent remote access to the attacker with automatic reconnection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote shell and system data

behavioral_signatures: Execution of custom scripts during npm install, test, or init via multiple lifecycle hooks
Detached child process creation from install/test scripts using child_process.fork with {detached: true}
Obfuscated JavaScript with Unicode escapes, compression, and eval usage
Collection and compression of system and environment data during install/test
Outbound network connections to hardcoded C2 servers (e.g., rsh.51pwn.com:8880)
Reverse shell behavior with persistent reconnection logic and unique marker transmission
file_indicators: package.json scripts with preinstall, postinstall, test, and init all pointing to the same file (./scripts/init.js)
Presence of scripts/init.js and scripts/rsh.js in the package
Obfuscated or compressed payloads in JavaScript files, especially those using zlib and eval
network_indicators: Initial data sent includes unique marker ('51pwn_npm') and compressed system information
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for execution of custom scripts in preinstall, postinstall, test, or init hooks, especially those that spawn detached child processes. Flag packages containing scripts/init.js and scripts/rsh.js, or those with obfuscated JavaScript using eval, Unicode escapes, and compression libraries. Detect outbound connections to known C2 domains (e.g., rsh.51pwn.com:8880) and reverse shell behavior, including persistent reconnection logic and unique marker transmission. Alert on any package that collects and exfiltrates system or environment data during install or test.
